source: It is false that, if this promise is genuine, this commitment is optional. Hence this promise is genuine and this commitment is not optional.

reconstruction.title: Negation of Conditional Implies Conjunction of Antecedent and Negated Consequent

claims.text: It is false that, if this promise is genuine, this commitment is optional.

evidence.quote: It is false that, if this promise is genuine, this commitment is optional.

claims.interpretation_note: This negates the conditional statement 'If this promise is genuine, then this commitment is optional.' In classical logic, ¬(P→Q) is equivalent to P∧¬Q.

claims.text: This promise is genuine and this commitment is not optional.

evidence.quote: Hence this promise is genuine and this commitment is not optional.

claims.interpretation_note: This is the logical consequence of the negated conditional in c1.

translations.reason: The negation of the conditional 'If P then Q' is logically equivalent to 'P and not Q' in classical logic.
This directly expresses the conjunction of the antecedent and negated consequent derived from the negated conditional in c1.

interpretation_notes: The argument relies on the classical equivalence ¬(P→Q) ≡ P∧¬Q. The translation preserves this structure using propositional logic formulas.
No quantifiers or predicates are needed since the claims are purely propositional.
